summary: This work demonstrates software compensation of trigger-synchronous coherent errors in trapped-ion qubits and qudits by measuring AC mains-induced magnetic-field perturbations and updating control pulse frequencies and phases to track instantaneous transition frequencies. The compensation reduces AC line-induced detuning by $21(9)\times$ and phase amplitude below measurement uncertainty, recovers single-qubit gate fidelity of $99.93(1)\%$ in randomized benchmarking, and improves Bernstein–Vazirani success probability from $10(7)\%$ to $70(9)\%$ in a 16-level system.
motivation: Trapped-ion systems and other quantum platforms experience reproducible, time-dependent coherent disturbances synchronized to external triggers (e.g., AC mains at 60 Hz), which act as deterministic control-frame errors rather than stochastic noise. Software-based compensation avoids the need for additional physical shielding, coils, or feedback hardware.
method: Line-trigger-referenced calibration of the magnetic-field perturbation $\Delta B(t)$ is used to derive pulse-by-pulse updates: programmed oscillator frequency $\omega_L^{(\mathrm{prog})}_j = \omega_0 + 2\pi\kappa_j\Delta B(t_j)$ ensures resonance, while phase correction $\phi_j^{(\mathrm{comp})} = \int_0^{t_j}\Delta B(t')\mathrm{d}t' - t_j\Delta B(t_j)$ (scaled by magnetic-field sensitivity $\kappa_j$) tracks accumulated phase evolution. The protocol extends naturally to multilevel qudits using transition-specific sensitivities.
result: Direct Ramsey measurements show harmonic detuning amplitude reduced by $8(1)\times$ and harmonic phase amplitude by $5(1)\times$. Randomized benchmarking on a $^{137}\mathrm{Ba}^+$ ion with $\kappa \approx 3.2$ MHz/G recovers $F_{\mathrm{avg}} = 99.93(1)\%$ with compensation enabled, matching the magnetic-field-insensitive reference qubit. Qudit algorithms show robustness across dimensions when compensation is applied.
